units.fit_note: Offers sample statements; does not require a syllabus statement. | Offers sample statements rather than requiring a syllabus statement.

units.passage: Clearly defining what constitutes acceptable AI use in coursework helps maintain academic integrity while guiding students in ethical AI practices they can carry into their careers.
units.why: 'Clearly defining what constitutes acceptable AI use in coursework' is an instruction to instructors to state expectations; P09.
units.fit_note: Recommends defining acceptable use in coursework; does not require a syllabus statement. | Phrased as a benefit and good practice, not a mandate.

units.passage: Instructor Tip: Include a statement in your syllabus about AI use, specifying whether, when, and how students may use AI tools in assignments.
units.why: 'Include a statement in your syllabus about AI use, specifying whether, when, and how students may use AI tools' recommends an AI syllabus statement, so P09.

units.passage: Providing explicit guidance in syllabi and assignment instructions helps students navigate these differences and develop adaptability—an essential skill in workplaces where AI policies and practices vary.
units.why: 'Providing explicit guidance in syllabi and assignment instructions helps students navigate these differences' recommends explicit written guidance, so P09.

units.passage: include an “AI use” section on all assignment instructions, and provide examples of acceptable and unacceptable use in your course.
units.why: Tip: 'include an AI use section on all assignment instructions, and provide examples of acceptable and unacceptable use', P09 per-assignment statement.

units.passage: set clear expectations with your students on how AI may or may not be used in assignments.
units.why: "set clear expectations with your students on how AI may or may not be used in assignments" tells instructors to communicate the rule per assignment, so P09 fits.

units.passage: Syllabi will include a statement about acce ptable use of AI in the course
units.why: "Syllabi will include a statement about acceptable use of AI in the course" requires an AI statement in every syllabus, P09.

units.passage: All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI.
units.why: "All course syllabi at UNT should include clear guidance as to permissible use of AI" asks every syllabus to state AI expectations (P09).

units.passage: Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions for course assignments and assessments related to the use of generative AI are key to compliance with the standards of academic integrity.
units.why: "Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions ... are key to compliance" explains why instructors should spell out AI rules for assignments and assessments; it extends the syllabus-statement expectation (P09).
units.fit_note: It extends the syllabus duty to assignment and assessment instructions and states the compliance rationale.

units.passage: Instructors should clearly communicate to students the permitted uses of generative AI in coursework. This communication should be written in the syllabus, assignment guidelines, and conveyed verbally in class
units.why: "Instructors should clearly communicate to students the permitted uses of generative AI in coursework" asks every instructor to state AI rules in writing and verbally; a statement of expectations is P09.
units.fit_note: Also names the channels: syllabus, assignment guidelines and verbal explanation in class.

units.passage: Instructors should specify expectations in their syllabus, helping students make a connection between their AI policies and course learning outcomes
units.why: "Instructors should specify expectations in their syllabus, helping students make a connection between their AI policies and course learning outcomes" requires a syllabus statement tied to outcomes, P09.
units.fit_note: Adds that the syllabus should link the AI policy to course learning outcomes.

units.passage: All instructors are required to refer to Northeastern’s Academic Integrity Policy in their course syllabi
units.why: "All instructors are required to refer to Northeastern's Academic Integrity Policy in their course syllabi" is a syllabus requirement, but about the integrity policy and not AI statements (P09).
units.fit_note: Requires a reference to the integrity policy, not an AI statement. / Requires reference to the Academic Integrity Policy, not a course-specific AI statement.

units.passage: Provide and discuss clear syllabus policy statements that define permitted and prohibited use in your courses; developed in collaboration with our instructional designers, we offer sample syllabi statements to use as a starting point in offering guidance to students, which may be modified to fit specific course or assignment needs
units.why: Instructors are directed to "Provide and discuss clear syllabus policy statements that define permitted and prohibited use", a duty to state AI expectations in the syllabus, so P09.
units.fit_note: Also asks instructors to discuss the statements with students (P66), not only to put them in the syllabus.

units.passage: Expectations for AI use should be clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials.
units.why: "Expectations for AI use should be clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials" asks that AI expectations be stated in syllabi and assignments, which is P09.

units.passage: Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule.
units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule" asks instructors to state their own AI rule, which is P09; it also rejects a single university rule.

units.passage: Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions.
units.why: "Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions" requires an AI statement in the syllabus or assignment, so P09.

units.passage: Faculty are encouraged to specify: What tools are allowed or discouraged What disclosure is required How student work will be evaluated
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to specify what tools are allowed or discouraged, what disclosure is required, and how student work will be evaluated.
units.why: Faculty "are encouraged to specify" tools, disclosure and evaluation, which asks instructors to state concrete expectations (P09).

units.passage: Instructors who allow students to use AI should clearly describe in their course policies how students may and may not use AI to support or augment their own work
units.why: Instructors who allow AI 'should clearly describe in their course policies how students may and may not use AI'. This requires stating expectations in the course policy, so P09.
units.fit_note: Applies only to instructors who allow AI, not to every syllabus.

units.passage: Given the various ways AI is embedded in research and writing tools, it will be important for instructors to be clear about whether AI may be used to support coursework.
units.why: The sentence says 'it will be important for instructors to be clear about whether AI may be used to support coursework'. This asks instructors to state expectations, so P09 (course-start, should); the mention of AI 'embedded in research and writing tools' is the reason, not a rule on built-in AI, so P07 does not fit as well.
units.fit_note: Gives AI embedded in research and writing tools as the reason instructors must be clear.

units.passage: In all cases, the instructor's responsibility is to communicate to students the expectations for their course.
units.why: Instructors must tell students their course expectations: 'responsibility is to communicate'. P09 (state AI expectations) fits; no syllabus is named, so a small gap.
units.fit_note: Does not say where (syllabus) the expectations are stated. / Does not specify the syllabus or assignment instructions as the place.

units.passage: Be explicit with students about your expectations regarding the use of ChatGPT and related AI tools for assignments, exams, and in the classroom, and be clear that engaging in unauthorized use of generative AI will be considered a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: Instructors should 'be explicit with students about your expectations' for assignments, exams and class: communicate AI rules (P09).
units.fit_note: Covers assignments, exams and classroom, not only the syllabus.

units.passage: Consider adding a specific statement in your syllabus and on Canvas regarding the use of AI tools
units.why: Instructors are advised to add 'a specific statement in your syllabus and on Canvas': syllabus AI statement (P09, as a recommendation).

units.passage: A clear AI policy in your syllabus takes away the guesswork.
units.why: "A clear AI policy in your syllabus takes away the guesswork": the reason for stating a policy in the syllabus; nearest P09, but it is a rationale.
units.fit_note: Gives the reason for a syllabus statement rather than requiring it.

units.passage: State your general stance and the rationale tied to learning outcomes in your syllabus; note privacy considerations.
units.why: Course level: "State your general stance and the rationale tied to learning outcomes in your syllabus": a syllabus statement, P09. The rationale tied to learning outcomes is part of the same instruction.
units.fit_note: Also asks for the rationale tied to learning outcomes (P83).

units.passage: Specify what’s allowed for this task (with examples), what must be cited, and the required disclosure format.
units.why: Assignment level: "Specify what's allowed for this task (with examples), what must be cited, and the required disclosure format": per-assignment instructions, P09.
units.fit_note: Per-assignment specification, not syllabus.

units.passage: Communicate your policy clearly in your syllabus
units.why: "Communicate your policy clearly in your syllabus and on the first day of class": communicate expectations, P09.
units.fit_note: Also first day of class.

units.passage: Effectively integrating Generative AI requires both proactive conversations with students and a clear syllabus policy.
units.why: The page states "Effectively integrating Generative AI requires both proactive conversations with students and a clear syllabus policy", asking for a syllabus AI statement (P09).
units.fit_note: Pairs a syllabus policy with proactive student conversations; a recommendation, not a mandate.

units.passage: Put your policy in places that are prominent or easy to see rather than hidden in a paragraph that includes other items. For example, place your policy near the front of the syllabus or somewhere near your sections on plagiarism and citation.
units.why: 'place your policy near the front of the syllabus' advises how to write the syllabus, which is done before the course, so before-course; P09 (AI statement in the syllabus), should.
units.fit_note: Concerns placement and prominence of the syllabus statement rather than requiring one.

units.passage: Where relevant, include a discussion of Generative AI tools in the descriptions or instructions for individual assignments.
units.why: "include a discussion of Generative AI tools in the descriptions or instructions" asks for assignment-level AI statements (P09, which includes assignment instructions).

units.passage: Be clear with students, both verbally and in written policies, as to when it is appropriate to use these tools for your courses and whether and how they should disclose that they used them.
units.why: "Be clear with students, both verbally and in written policies, as to when it is appropriate to use these tools" asks for explicit rules (P09).
units.fit_note: Also says the statement should cover whether and how students disclose AI use.

units.passage: Clear syllabus language must specify how the use of GenAI tools, programs or computer-based information affects the standard of honest scholarship.
units.why: "Clear syllabus language must specify how the use of GenAI tools ... affects the standard of honest scholarship" is a duty (A require, B neutral); require, following the duty convention.

units.passage: Faculty are likewise obliged to communicate those policies to students at the onset of the semester, preferably in the syllabus.
units.why: "Faculty are likewise obliged to communicate those policies to students at the onset of the semester" is a duty (A require, B neutral); require.

units.passage: Adopt a GenAI policy for your course and include that policy in your syllabus.
units.why: "Adopt a GenAI policy for your course and include that policy in your syllabus" is a duty under Instructor Requirements (A require, B neutral); require.

units.passage: A syllabus statement, when paired with acceptable GenAI use guidelines, provides clarity by establishing a common language and framework for both faculty and students
units.why: Describes pairing a syllabus statement with use guidelines for a common language: P09 (informs).

units.passage: Ensure that your syllabus contains a statement relating to the Honor Code and permissions regarding the usage of artificial intelligence (AI).
units.policy: Faculty ensure that the syllabus contains a statement relating to the Honor Code and permissions regarding the usage of artificial intelligence (AI).
units.why: Faculty are told to 'Ensure that your syllabus contains a statement relating to the Honor Code and permissions regarding the usage of artificial intelligence'. That is an instruction to include an AI statement in the syllabus, so P09 with modality 'should' (framed as a tip) addressed to instructors.

units.passage: Education Developer, Dr. Lance Eaton, has collected sample syllabi statements for Generative AI tools by discipline.
units.policy: Faculty are directed to a collection of sample syllabus statements for generative AI tools by discipline.
units.why: Faculty are pointed to a collection of sample syllabus statements by discipline. It is a pointer to help instructors write their statements, which is support for faculty in setting policy, nearest P63 (support faculty in learning AI) though it is sample statements, not workshops.
units.fit_note: Offers sample statements as a resource rather than requiring one.

units.passage: Assignment prompts, especially for papers or other written assessments, should include specific parameters for AI usage. Specific prompts can help deter and detect unauthorized tool use (University of Southern California, n.d.).
units.policy: Assignment prompts, especially for papers or other written assessments, should include specific parameters for AI usage.
units.why: Assignment prompts 'should include specific parameters for AI usage', especially for written work. This asks instructors to state AI rules in assignment instructions, matching P09, which includes assignment instructions.

units.passage: The CTLA recommends instructors establish a course policy on student use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), and staff have created three versions of a policy reflecting varying levels of acceptable GenAI use by students.
units.why: CTLA 'recommends instructors establish a course policy', which asks instructors to put an AI rule in the course; P09 fits because it is about stating expectations in the course, though it says 'recommends' rather than requires.
units.fit_note: It is a recommendation, not a requirement, and speaks of a course policy rather than specifically the syllabus.

units.passage: The CTLA recommends instructors establish a course policy on student use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), and staff have created versions of a policy reflecting varying levels of acceptable GenAI use by students.
units.why: The CTLA 'recommends instructors establish a course policy': P09.
units.fit_note: It is a recommendation, not a requirement.

units.passage: The Committee on Academic Misconduct (COAM) recommends that every faculty member, instructor, and graduate teaching associate who is teaching a course prepare and distribute (or make available) to all students a course syllabus that contains a statement concerning "academic misconduct" or "academic integrity".
units.why: COAM "recommends that every faculty member, instructor, and graduate teaching associate" prepare a syllabus statement on "academic misconduct"; it asks for a syllabus statement, which is P09 (here about integrity in general, with AI in a separate section).
units.fit_note: The recommended statement is on academic misconduct generally; AI appears in a separate section.

units.passage: Instead, faculty are encouraged to make intentional, discipline-appropriate choices and to communicate those choices clearly to students.
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to communicate their AI choices clearly to students.
units.why: Faculty are told 'to communicate those choices clearly to students', which is about making expectations explicit at the start; closest is P09 though it does not say in the syllabus specifically.
units.fit_note: Does not say the statement must be in the syllabus; only that choices be communicated clearly. | Asks instructors to communicate their choices clearly to students but does not name the syllabus.

units.passage: Generative AI Policy (required component, text may vary and could be included, as long as it is explicit, in Academic Integrity Language)
units.why: The heading calls a Generative AI policy a 'required component' of the syllabus, which may sit in academic-integrity language if explicit; this is a syllabus-statement requirement (P09).

units.passage: If you would like to restrict the usage of Generative AI in the class, we encourage you to either integrate this policy into your academic integrity statement or to have a stand-alone Generative AI usage policy.
units.why: Advises placing the policy in the integrity statement or a stand-alone policy; about where to state AI rules in the syllabus (P09).

units.passage: I will clearly state this on any relevant assignment.
units.why: Instructor commits to stating in the assignment when AI is prohibited; per-assignment communication (P09).
units.fit_note: Assignment-level rather than syllabus-level statement.

units.passage: I will never use Generative AI to grade your work or to communicate with you. Example AI Policy: Full Generative AI Usage If you would like your students to openly explore Generative AI usage within your course, we still encourage that you have a clear policy so that students are supported in knowing how to use Generative AI, as this is an emerging skill.
units.why: Even for open use, instructors are encouraged to 'have a clear policy'; this is a statement that AI use is an emerging skill needing explicit rules (P09).

units.passage: We encourage you to be explicit in each assignment about what they can use Generative AI to do and how you want them to acknowledge their Generative AI usage.
units.why: Instructors encouraged to say per assignment what AI may do and how to acknowledge it; per-assignment AI statement (P09).

units.passage: Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi, outlining how AI tools can be used in the course. Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided below.
units.why: Faculty 'should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi', which is a syllabus-statement expectation (P09).

units.passage: Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse.
units.why: Faculty should 'Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse'; P09 is the nearest communicating-expectations type, but this adds consequences.
units.fit_note: Also asks to communicate consequences of misuse, not only to include a syllabus statement. / Also requires communicating consequences of misuse, not only expectations.

units.passage: Update your course syllabus honor code based on your decision to use or not use AICGTs.
units.why: Faculty should 'Update your course syllabus honor code based on your decision to use or not use AICGTs', a syllabus statement expectation (P09).

units.passage: Clarify your expectations regarding academic honesty. Be clear about what your students may or may not use.
units.why: 'Clarify your expectations regarding academic honesty. Be clear about what your students may or may not use.' (P09, communicating what is permitted).

units.passage: Please note that ODU does not require an AI statement in your syllabus, but it is highly recommended.
units.why: 'ODU does not require an AI statement in your syllabus, but it is highly recommended' states no mandate but a recommendation (P09, with fit note).
units.fit_note: No requirement; recommended only. / Explicitly says the statement is not required, only highly recommended.

units.passage: Have a syllabus policy statement on what AI use is allowed, decided at your own or your unit's discretion based on the course's learning objectives.
units.policy: Instructors have a syllabus policy statement on what AI use is allowed
units.why: "Have a syllabus policy statement on what AI use is allowed" is an imperative to instructors listed under baseline responsibilities, so it is a must for instructors that every syllabus carry an AI statement (P09), set before the course.

units.passage: Every UO syllabus should say something about GenAI.
units.why: "Every UO syllabus should say something about GenAI" is a university-level should that all syllabi carry an AI statement (P09), communicated at course start.

units.passage: Students move between courses with very different AI policies. Say what's allowed on the syllabus and in assignment instructions, and be ready to explain your reasoning if asked.
units.why: "Say what's allowed on the syllabus and in assignment instructions" tells instructors to state expectations in both places, which fits P09.

units.passage: A syllabus statement isn't enough on its own. Research suggests students need to see AI expectations at the assignment level, not just the course level.
units.why: "A syllabus statement isn't enough on its own" and students "need to see AI expectations at the assignment level" tell instructors to state AI expectations in assignments as well, a P09 rule.
units.fit_note: Extends the syllabus-statement duty to assignment-level statements.

units.passage: ensure faculty set clear course policies on AI use, receive feedback on their approaches, and, ultimately, have their work to adapt courses made visible in evaluation;
units.policy: UO teaching expectations are AI aware: faculty set clear course policies on AI use and receive feedback on their approaches
units.why: The Council's first priority outcome is that 'faculty set clear course policies on AI use, receive feedback on their approaches'; it addresses the university (admin) as a recommendation to ensure (should), over-time, and matches the syllabus-statement type P09 in requiring a course AI policy.
units.fit_note: Also says faculty receive feedback and that adaptation work is made visible in evaluation. / Recommendation framed as an outcome the Council seeks, not an instruction to faculty; the evaluation part is a separate unit.

units.passage: These changes take effect immediately and I encourage you to incorporate these definitions into your course syllabus and in discussions with students about academic misconduct.
units.policy: Instructors incorporate the plagiarism definitions into their course syllabus and in discussions with students
units.why: The letter urges instructors to "incorporate these definitions into your course syllabus and in discussions with students", a syllabus statement rule (P09).
units.fit_note: Also asks for discussion with students (P66).

units.passage: I join with the Office of the Provost in encouraging all faculty to consider and determine your own course philosophy and expectations around the use of generative AI tools for each of your courses, communicate those expectations in your course syllabus, and discuss them in the first week of the term.
units.policy: Faculty communicate their generative AI expectations in the course syllabus
units.why: Faculty should "communicate those expectations in your course syllabus", the syllabus statement rule (P09).

units.passage: All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy that communicates expectations for student use of artificial intelligence.
units.why: This is a syllabus requirement addressed to course syllabi: 'All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy'. It is a P09 type rule because it mandates an AI statement in every syllabus, binds instructors, and is a before-course design duty.

units.passage: Add the GenAI syllabus statement to their syllabi, tailoring it with details of the specific approach to the use of GenAI in the course
units.policy: Instructors are strongly encouraged to add the GenAI syllabus statement to their syllabi, tailoring it with details of the specific approach to the use of GenAI in the course.
units.why: Instructors are 'strongly encouraged' to follow the guidance and add the GenAI syllabus statement, tailored to the course. This recommends putting an AI statement in the syllabus, so P09 with should.
units.fit_note: Encouraged this term, not yet required; the statement is to be tailored to the course.

units.passage: All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy that communicates expectations for student use of artificial intelligence. Determination of permitted or prohibited AI use remains at the discretion of the instructor. See also OSU's Syllabus Minimum Requirements Policy
units.why: 'All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy' requires an AI statement in every syllabus, so P09 with must, addressed to instructors.

units.passage: Be sure to use both the visual indicator and a detailed description of the specific application of this policy, both in the syllabus and in any assignment-specific language.
units.why: 'Be sure to use both the visual indicator and a detailed description' since 'Using the visual indicator alone is not fully accessible' tells instructors how to communicate the tier: P09.
units.fit_note: Also an accessibility reason: icons alone are not accessible. | Adds that icons alone are not accessible and that detail must also appear in assignment language.

units.passage: Students encounter different policies across their courses and need specific detail to help them understand your approach to AI in the course.
units.why: 'Students encounter different policies across their courses and need specific detail' is the reason for detailed statements; one course's policy is not another's: P11.
units.fit_note: Gives the reason detailed statements are needed (policies differ across courses), not a duty itself.

units.passage: Clear, detailed, transparent statements also help to hold students accountable in student conduct proceedings.
units.why: 'Clear, detailed, transparent statements also help to hold students accountable in student conduct proceedings' links statement detail to enforcement; P09 as the statement-writing rule.

units.passage: Examples of specific tasks for which students may be allowed to use AI
units.policy: Instructors should include examples of specific tasks for which students may be allowed to use AI: generate ideas, polish or edit drafted text, create an outline of an essay, modify or design presentation slides, review content, self-quizzing, or other studying purposes.
units.why: Instructors should list 'Examples of specific tasks for which students may be allowed to use AI' such as generating ideas, self-quizzing, outlining. This is guidance on spelling out permitted uses in the syllabus, so P09.
units.fit_note: Lists example allowed tasks (ideas, editing, outline, slides, review, self-quizzing) for instructors to name; it is advice on statement content as well as permitted uses. | The content lists permitted uses (ideas, editing, outlining, self-quizzing); P09 captures only the duty to specify.

units.passage: AI tools that you do or do not want students to use, if specific examples should be called out.
units.why: Instructors should name 'AI tools that you do or do not want students to use, if specific examples should be called out'. Statement content: P09.

units.passage: OSU's Syllabus Minimum Requirements Policy states that "A ll course syllabi must include an AI usage policy that communicates expectations for student use of artificial intelligence. Determination of permitted or prohibited AI use remains at the discretion of the instructor.
units.why: The page quotes the policy that 'All course syllabi must include an AI usage policy', a P09 requirement, and ties it to instructor discretion.

units.passage: The Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) supports an ethic of transparency around the use of generative AI in teaching and learning, and encourages you to develop and share a course-level AI policy statement in your syllabus.
units.why: CTL 'encourages you to develop and share a course-level AI policy statement in your syllabus' and supports 'transparency'. A recommendation to put the policy in the syllabus: P09, should.

units.passage: All OSU course syllabi are required to include a link to the Student Conduct Expectations regardless of the particular course AI policy.
units.why: 'All OSU course syllabi are required to include a link to the Student Conduct Expectations regardless of the particular course AI policy'. A syllabus content rule that connects AI to conduct: P09.
units.fit_note: Required content is a conduct link, not an AI statement. | Requires a conduct-code link in every syllabus, not an AI statement itself.

units.passage: Once your course policy is articulated, be sure assignment and assessment directions are in alignment with your course policy
units.why: 'be sure assignment and assessment directions are in alignment with your course policy' asks for consistency between the syllabus and assignments; nearest is P09, as a duty to state the policy at assignment level.
units.fit_note: Asks for consistency between statement and assignment instructions, an extension of the syllabus-statement type. | Asks that assignment directions match the course AI policy, not only that a syllabus statement exist.

units.passage: it is important for instructors to provide students with clear guidelines similar to the guidelines on collaboration , on the use of AI within coursework, and when and how the use of AI within a course should be cited.
units.why: Instructors should "provide students with clear guidelines ... on the use of AI within coursework, and when and how the use of AI within a course should be cited", a duty to state AI expectations (P09).

units.passage: Stating general policies in your syllabus as well as addressing specific expectations that pertain to individual assignments throughout the semester will help students understand what they can and cannot do and why.
units.why: "Stating general policies in your syllabus as well as addressing specific expectations that pertain to individual assignments" asks for AI expectations in syllabus and assignments (P09).

units.passage: You may either create a standalone AI policy or add a statement about AI to the academic integrity policy already in your syllabus and on Canvas.
units.why: "You may either create a standalone AI policy or add a statement about AI to the academic integrity policy already in your syllabus" tells instructors to put AI in the syllabus (P09).
units.fit_note: Gives the choice between standalone and integrated syllabus statements.

units.passage: When introducing a particular assignment, be sure to clarify any specific AI-related expectations beyond your general policy.
units.why: "be sure to clarify any specific AI-related expectations beyond your general policy" tells instructors to state assignment-level AI rules (P09).

units.passage: It also encourages faculty to proactively redesign assignments and clearly communicate AI expectations to promote honest student effort and responsible use of AI tools.
units.why: Faculty are encouraged to 'clearly communicate AI expectations', a communication-of-expectations rule (P09), here not tied to the syllabus specifically.
units.fit_note: Encourages communicating expectations without naming the syllabus. | Calls for communicating expectations but does not name the syllabus as the place.

units.passage: This faculty guide serves as a checklist for faculty as they think about how to prepare to teach in the Age of AI. The list includes steps like including a syllabus statement about AI, testing out AI tools, and testing assessments in an AI tool.
units.why: The checklist lists 'including a syllabus statement about AI' as a preparation step, which is P09 (AI statement in the syllabus).
units.fit_note: A checklist item, not a mandate.

units.passage: Senate Policy 43-00 requires course instructors to provide students with a course syllabus that includes the academic integrity policy for the course
units.why: Senate Policy 43-00 'requires course instructors to provide students with a course syllabus that includes the academic integrity policy', the base that makes AI rules appear in syllabi; P09 with a note that the rule is not AI-specific.
units.fit_note: The requirement is for an academic integrity statement, not specifically for AI.

units.passage: Faculty are required to state their expectations for academic honesty as part of the grading policy in every course.
units.why: 'Faculty are required to state their expectations for academic honesty... in every course' requires a syllabus integrity statement; AI is not named here, so the fit is partial.
units.fit_note: A required academic-honesty statement; it does not mention AI. | The required statement is about academic honesty generally; AI is the next sentence.

units.passage: Educators can find customizable language around student’s use of AI in the ‘Faculty Resources’ section of the University’s Academic Integrity Resources page
units.why: Points educators to 'customizable language around student's use of AI' for syllabi, a syllabus-statement resource (P09).
units.fit_note: Offers statement language; does not require it. | Only points to template AI language; no requirement is stated.

units.passage: Faculty are also encouraged to list details on acceptable use or restrictions of using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the course policies section of the syllabus.
units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to list details on acceptable use or restrictions of using Artificial Intelligence (AI)' in the syllabus, a recommended AI syllabus statement: P09.

units.passage: Be clear in what is allowed or prohibited, and any conditions such as citations, limitations in scope, limitations by specific product, etc.
units.policy: Instructors should be clear about what is allowed or prohibited and any conditions, such as citations, limitations in scope, or limitations by specific product.
units.why: "Be clear in what is allowed or prohibited, and any conditions" tells instructors to state expectations explicitly, which is P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus) with modality should.
units.fit_note: Recommends clarity and conditions rather than requiring a statement (coder B).

units.passage: Communicate your values and expectations.
